niche.habitat: Subsurface NH3-H2O eutectic oceans, near hydrothermal vent fields
niche.diet: Chemosynthetic grazers, smaller swimmers, ammonia-rich brine fauna

body: Streamlined, fluid-filled body; laminated iron-nickel carapace; electroreceptive rostrum; jaw-thoracic resonator

links: Prevents tissue collapse under crush pressure
Physical root: High surface pressure and fluid mechanics

skill.effect: The creature's fluid-filled body naturally equalizes with its surroundings, allowing it to withstand crushing depths and harsh environments without strain. It lands from great heights with a soft, cushioned grace that avoids injury.

chains.weakness: Rapid temperature changes cause thermal stress; heat sources attract predators.

journal.en: A knife of bone and iron in the blue dark.

plausibility.summary: At ~40 bar (F5), gas-filled spaces would implode; pressure-matched fluid compartments (F16) are the standard deep/high-pressure solution and avoid swim-bladder pathology when moving through pressure gradients in vent-connected brines.
fixes: At ~40 bar (F5), gas-filled spaces would implode; pressure-matched fluid compartments (F16) are the standard deep/high-pressure solution and avoid swim-bladder pathology when moving through pressure gradients in vent-connected brines.

analogues.organism: Hadal amphipods and abyssal fishes lacking gas swim bladders; gelatinous deep-sea fauna with isotonic/internal pressure support
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Hunts in total darkness of deep brine
Physical root: Metal-rich crust and reducing chemistry

skill.effect: Its sensitive snout twitches and hums when near concealed treasures or disguised foes, causing their hidden forms to shimmer into view. The creature instinctively focuses on vulnerable spots, making them glow faintly for easy targeting.

chains.weakness: Strong electromagnetic fields scramble detection; magnetic interference causes disorientation.

plausibility.summary: Split ‘Ore Sense’ into (1) prey galvanic detection—plausible—and (2) vent-brine redox/ionic ‘ore proximity’ sensing within ~meters, not passive EM from silent rock.
fixes: Split ‘Ore Sense’ into (1) prey galvanic detection—plausible—and (2) vent-brine redox/ionic ‘ore proximity’ sensing within ~meters, not passive EM from silent rock.

analogues.organism: Great white shark (Carcharodon carcharias) ampullae of Lorenzini; platypus (Ornithorhynchus anatinus) bill electroreception
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Physical root: Sound propagation in dense atmosphere/fluid

skill.effect: The creature emits a sharp, resonant click that echoes through the area, freezing nearby foes in place for a short while and exposing their hidden locations. The powerful sound waves ripple outward, visibly shaking the ground and leaving opponents disoriented and vulnerable.

chains.weakness: Soft terrain absorbs sound; silent prey or sound-dampening fields evade detection.

journal.en: The dark is just a shape it knows.

plausibility.summary: Echolocation in opaque fluid is favored where vision fails; NH₃–H₂O brines (F10) support sound transmission with different absorption than air but remain usable at short–medium range for ambush predators. Thoracic/jaw coupling matches F14’s resonator logic extended into subsurface media.
fixes: Echolocation in opaque fluid is favored where vision fails; NH₃–H₂O brines (F10) support sound transmission with different absorption than air but remain usable at short–medium range for ambush predators. Thoracic/jaw coupling matches F14’s resonator logic extended into subsurface media.

analogues.organism: Bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) and other odontocetes: narrowband clicks for high-resolution sonar in turbid water
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Physical root: Super-Earth gravity and metal bioavailability

skill.effect: Its layered, metal-reinforced carapace deflects incoming strikes with a heavy, clanging resonance, absorbing blows that would otherwise pierce through. The creature braces firmly against attacks, causing sharp impacts to shatter harmlessly against its unyielding armor.

chains.weakness: Inlays fatigue after repeated impact; heavy attacks cause structural cracks.

journal.en: Armored against the weight of worlds.

plausibility.summary: 1.35 g (F3) raises skeletal stresses; localized Fe–Ni along growth laminae (F17) from vent-available metals (F11) is convergent with bio-scavenged reinforcement without making the whole exoskeleton metallic. Fatigue at inlays after repeated impact is realistic.
fixes: 1.35 g (F3) raises skeletal stresses; localized Fe–Ni along growth laminae (F17) from vent-available metals (F11) is convergent with bio-scavenged reinforcement without making the whole exoskeleton metallic. Fatigue at inlays after repeated impact is realistic.

relations.note: (council kind 'Predator') Hidrazón may snatch juvenile Eridians near vent shafts; Eridians use sonic lures to deter them.

temperament: Ambush predator; solitary; highly territorial via acoustic maps
secrets: Hidrazón blood is a super-conductive brine; can craft high-efficiency electrical conduits.
Eating Hidrazón meat grants temporary pressure resistance but causes ammonia toxicity over time.
moments: In the black water, a flash of bio-electric blue illuminates a snout filled with needle-teeth; the sound of a clicker click echoes like a gunshot in the fluid.

journal.en: The deep ocean is a cathedral of pressure.
We build our walls high; the Hidrazón builds its teeth.
